eligibility.income_note: Income-tested on adjusted family net income

programmes.source_snippet: This grant helps low- to moderate-income seniors with the cost of their property taxes.

programmes.funder: Government of Ontario (Ministry of Health / Public Health Units)
programmes.amount_note: Free preventive, routine and emergency dental care for children and youth 17 and under from low-income households; also covers emergency care stream for urgent dental needs.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online, by mail or through your local public health unit
Receive the HSO card and visit a participating dental provider

eligibility.income_note: No dollar figure is published on the ontario.ca pages; they state only that the child must be in a household that meets the income eligibility requirements and refer applicants to ServiceOntario or the local public health unit.

programmes.source_snippet: Healthy Smiles Ontario is a government-funded dental program that provides free preventive, routine, and emergency dental services for children and youth 17 years old and under from low-income households.

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt pour les personnes et les familles à faible revenu
programmes.name_en: Low-Income Individuals and Families Tax (LIFT) Credit
programmes.amount_note: Non-refundable Ontario tax credit of up to $875 per person ($1,750 per couple) that reduces or eliminates Ontario income tax for low-income workers.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual Ontario tax return.

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return; the credit is calculated from employment income

documents_required.doc: Filed income tax return with employment income

eligibility.income_note: Full credit below ~$32,500 individual income; phases out by $50,000 ($65,000 family)

programmes.source_snippet: The LIFT credit provides up to $875 in Ontario personal income tax relief to tax filers who have employment income, including those earning minimum wage.

programmes.funder: Government of Canada and Government of Ontario
programmes.amount_note: Portable monthly rent subsidy (difference between 80% of average market rent and 30% of household income) for households on/eligible for the social housing waitlist; follows the household if it moves within Ontario.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply through your local service manager; funds limited per year.

procedure_steps.detail: Be on (or eligible for) the social housing waiting list via your local service manager
Apply for COHB through the service manager

eligibility.income_note: Household income limits set by the program (generally under local ceilings)

programmes.source_snippet: The COHB pays the difference between 30 per cent of the household's income and average market rent in the area, and is portable across Ontario.

programmes.amount_note: 36% discount on adult TTC single fares ($3.30 to $2.10) and 21% off the adult monthly pass ($156.00 to $123.25), programmed onto a PRESTO card for 12 months.
programmes.deadline_note: Discount valid 12 months; annual eligibility review/reapplication required from August 2026.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online on the City of Toronto Fair Pass page
Provide income documents or an OW/ODSP/Child Care Fee Subsidy program ID
Discount is loaded onto your PRESTO card; ride TTC/Wheel-Trans

documents_required.doc: Income documents or OW/ODSP/CCFS program ID

eligibility.income_note: Toronto sets Fair Pass eligibility at total after-tax family income below 75% of the Low-Income Measure After-Tax threshold; for a 1-person household this is $22,691 per year. Thresholds rise with household size.

programmes.source_snippet: The Fair Pass Transit Discount Program provides a full year of savings on TTC and Wheel-Trans trips by offering a 36 per cent discount on adult single fares and a 21 per cent discount on adult monthly passes.

programmes.name_en: City of Toronto Welcome Policy (recreation fee subsidy)
programmes.amount_note: Annual credit (recently about $641 for adults and $328 for children/youth, subject to change) applied to City recreation program registration fees for low-income Toronto residents.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before registering for recreation programs; approval valid for the calendar year.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for the Welcome Policy online or with staff support at a recreation centre
Once approved, register for City recreation programs using the subsidy credit

documents_required.doc: Income documents (Notice of Assessment or OW/ODSP statement)

eligibility.income_note: Family income below the LIM-based threshold (varies by household size)

programmes.source_snippet: The Welcome Policy provides a fee subsidy to help low-income individuals and families access City of Toronto recreation programs.

programmes.funder: Province of British Columbia (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: July 2026-June 2027: up to $1,750/year for the first child, $1,100 for the second, $900 for each additional child, plus up to $500/year single-parent supplement; paid monthly with the federal CCB.

procedure_steps.detail: Register for the Canada Child Benefit and file your income tax return
The B.C. Family Benefit is calculated and paid automatically with the CCB

eligibility.income_note: Full amount under $30,176 AFNI; reduced above, guaranteed minimum until $96,562, then phased to zero

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum annual benefit you may receive is: $1,750 for your first child; $1,100 for your second child; $900 for each additional child.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly cash payment toward rent for BC residents aged 60+ with low to moderate incomes who pay more than 30% of gross income toward rent; amount depends on income, rent and location.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to BC Housing online or by mail
Provide income and rent verification; reassessed annually

eligibility.income_note: Income and rent ceilings vary by community size

programmes.source_snippet: SAFER provides monthly cash payments to subsidize rents for eligible BC residents who are age 60 or over and pay rent for their homes.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly rent assistance for working low-income families with at least one dependent child; subsidy based on household size, income and rent paid in the private market.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to BC Housing online or by mail
Provide proof of income, rent and dependent children

eligibility.income_note: BC Housing states applicants must have a total before-tax annual household income of $60,000 or less. Other conditions apply: the household must have at least one dependent child, and meet employment-income and residency tests.

programmes.source_snippet: The Rental Assistance Program provides eligible low-income working families with cash assistance to help with their monthly rent payments.

programmes.funder: Province of British Columbia (Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction)
programmes.amount_note: Reduced-cost annual bus pass (Compass Card in Metro Vancouver / BC Transit pass elsewhere) for people on disability assistance and low-income seniors receiving the Seniors Supplement; $45 annual administration fee.
programmes.deadline_note: Renew each calendar year; the pass is valid January 1 to December 31.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through My Self Serve or call the ministry
Pay the $45 administration fee; pass is mailed/linked for the calendar year

documents_required.doc: Persons with Disabilities designation or low-income senior/Seniors Supplement status

eligibility.income_note: No income figure published on the B.C. government page; eligibility is defined by receipt of specific benefits — notably the federal Guaranteed Income Supplement for seniors 60+, or provincial disability/income assistance.

programmes.source_snippet: The BC Bus Pass Program offers a reduced cost, annual bus pass for low income seniors and individuals receiving disability assistance from the Province of British Columbia.

programmes.funder: Province of British Columbia (Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly assistance for people in need; a single employable person receives $1,060/month (support + shelter, 2024 rate), higher for couples/families and those with disabilities designation.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via My Self Serve or by phone
Complete the work search and eligibility interview

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested; earnings exemptions apply

programmes.source_snippet: B.C. Employment and Assistance provides help with essential living costs and employment services to British Columbians in need.

programmes.funder: Province of British Columbia (Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly assistance for people designated as Persons with Disabilities; a single person receives $1,483.50/month (2024 rate), plus supplements (e.g., bus pass, health supplements).

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for income assistance first (My Self Serve)
Complete the PWD designation application with a medical professional

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested (higher asset limit than regular income assistance); earnings exemption ~$16,200/year

programmes.source_snippet: Disability assistance can help you if you need financial or health support; you must be designated as a Person with Disabilities (PWD) to receive this type of assistance.

programmes.funder: Province of British Columbia (Ministry of Education and Child Care)
programmes.amount_note: Income-tested child care funding of up to $1,250/month per child (group infant/toddler care), on top of provider fee reductions and $10-a-day ChildCareBC sites; factors: income, family size, type of care.
programmes.deadline_note: Renew each year; report changes in income or care arrangements.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online with your BC Services Card
Provide child care provider information and income consent (CRA verification)

eligibility.income_note: Families earning up to $45,000 may get full funding; reduced amount up to about $111,000

programmes.source_snippet: The Affordable Child Care Benefit is a monthly payment to help eligible families with the cost of child care; factors like income, family size, and type of care determine how much families can get.

programmes.amount_note: Income-based drug coverage: families pay eligible prescription costs up to a deductible (0-3% of net income) and family maximum; PharmaCare pays the rest, including 100% after the maximum.

procedure_steps.detail: Register online or by phone with your Personal Health Number and CRA income consent

documents_required.doc: Personal Health Numbers for all family members

eligibility.income_note: All BC residents with MSP coverage eligible; deductible/maximum based on family net income (1939-born and earlier get enhanced assistance)

programmes.source_snippet: Fair PharmaCare helps B.C. families pay for eligible prescription drugs, dispensing fees and some medical supplies; the less a family earns, the more help they get.

programmes.amount_note: 2026: between $1,221 (minimum) and $3,068 (maximum) per child under 18, indexed each January; plus single-parent supplement (up to $1,077), school supplies supplement and handicapped child supplement; paid quarterly by default, monthly on request.

procedure_steps.detail: Birth registration with the Directeur de l'état civil usually triggers automatic enrolment
Newcomers/adoptive parents apply via Retraite Québec online services

eligibility.income_note: Income-tested above family net income thresholds; minimum amount paid regardless of income

programmes.source_snippet: Pour 2026, le montant maximal est de 3 068 $ par enfant par année, et le montant minimal est de 1 221 $ par enfant.

programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit for low-income Quebec residents combining QST, housing and northern village components; paid monthly if $800+, quarterly if $240-$799, annually if $240 or less (since July 2025). Amount depends on income, housing situation and family status.
programmes.deadline_note: Claim Schedule D with your Quebec tax return; register for direct deposit.

procedure_steps.detail: File your Quebec return and complete Schedule D
Tenants: keep the RL-31 slip from your landlord; homeowners: use the municipal tax account number

documents_required.doc: Filed Quebec income tax return with Schedule D

eligibility.income_note: Revenu Quebec publishes maximum family income figures for the July 2026 - June 2027 payment period: $64,545 for a person without a spouse and for a single-parent family (+$2,634 per dependent child), and $70,395 for a person with a spouse. At or above these amounts no credit is paid.

programmes.source_snippet: Le crédit d'impôt pour solidarité aide les personnes à faible revenu qui résident au Québec; depuis juillet 2025, la fréquence des versements varie selon le montant (mensuelle à partir de 800 $).

programmes.funder: Gouvernement du Québec (Ministère de la Famille)
programmes.amount_note: Reduced parental contribution of $9.35 per day per child (2025, indexed annually) at subsidized CPEs, daycare centres and home childcare; additional contribution for higher family incomes via the tax system.
programmes.deadline_note: Register on La Place 0-5 waiting list for a subsidized space.

procedure_steps.detail: Register your child on La Place 0-5 (centralized waiting list)
Accept a subsidized space; pay the reduced contribution directly to the provider

eligibility.income_note: Base reduced contribution is not income-tested; additional contribution applies above income thresholds via the tax return

programmes.source_snippet: Subsidized childcare in Quebec is offered at a reduced contribution set by the government and indexed annually ($9.35 per day in 2025).

programmes.name_en: Quebec Student Financial Assistance (Aide financière aux études - Loans and Bursaries)
programmes.funder: Gouvernement du Québec (Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur)
programmes.amount_note: Loans and needs-based bursaries (non-repayable) for full-time students; assessment based on allowable expenses minus contributions from student/parents/spouse; part-time and disability streams also exist.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply each award year; apply as soon as admission is confirmed.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via AFE online services
Provide income information (and parents'/spouse's) and confirm full-time enrolment

eligibility.income_note: Needs-tested on income and family situation

programmes.source_snippet: The Loans and Bursaries Program enables students with insufficient financial resources to pursue full-time secondary, college or university studies.

programmes.name_en: Quebec Social Assistance and Social Solidarity (last-resort financial assistance)
programmes.amount_note: 2026 monthly amounts (living independently): Social Assistance $845 (single, no constraints) / $1,283 (couple); Social Solidarity $1,318 (single with severely limited capacity for employment) / $1,934 (couple); indexed each January.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online, by phone or at a Services Québec office
Provide proof of financial situation and, for Solidarity, a medical report on employment constraints

eligibility.income_note: Strict income, asset and liquid-asset tests; some work income exempted

programmes.source_snippet: Aide sociale: personne seule 845 $ par mois; Solidarité sociale: personne seule 1 318 $ par mois (montants 2026, vivant à son compte).

programmes.funder: Gouvernement du Québec (Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale)
programmes.amount_note: Income replacement for maternity/paternity/parental/adoption leave in Quebec: basic plan pays 70% of weekly earnings for maternity (18 weeks) and 70%/55% for parental weeks (special plan pays 75% over a shorter period); maximum insurable earnings indexed annually.
programmes.deadline_note: Benefit choices (basic vs special plan) are irrevocable once payments begin.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at rqap.gouv.qc.ca after stopping work
Choose basic or special plan; share parental weeks between parents

documents_required.doc: Record of Employment or self-employment income proof

eligibility.income_note: Needs minimum insurable earnings (~$2,000) in the qualifying period; covers employees and self-employed

programmes.source_snippet: The Québec Parental Insurance Plan pays benefits to all eligible workers - salaried or self-employed - taking maternity, paternity, parental or adoption leave.

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt pour prime au travail
programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit encouraging low-income workers to stay in/return to the labour market; amounts depend on household work income and family situation (adapted work premium for people with severely limited capacity).
programmes.deadline_note: Claim with the Quebec tax return; advance payments available on request.

procedure_steps.detail: File your Quebec income tax return and claim the work premium

eligibility.income_note: Revenu Quebec's eligibility table for the 2025 taxation year requires annual family income below $24,475 for a person living alone; higher thresholds apply to couples and families with children, and the adapted work premium uses separate amounts.

programmes.source_snippet: The work premium is a refundable tax credit intended to encourage people to join or stay in the labour market.

programmes.name_en: Quebec Public Prescription Drug Insurance Plan (RAMQ)
programmes.funder: Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ)
programmes.amount_note: Mandatory public plan for Quebec residents without private drug coverage; annual premium via the tax return (max ~$731, indexed) with income-based exemptions, plus deductible/co-insurance capped monthly; free for children of insured parents, social assistance recipients and low-income seniors (GIS).

procedure_steps.detail: Register with RAMQ if not covered by a private plan
Pay the premium through your Quebec tax return; present your health card at the pharmacy

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling. RAMQ states that as a rule you qualify for the Public Prescription Drug Insurance Plan if you don't have access to a private plan — eligibility turns on absence of private coverage, not income; premiums and deductibles are scaled to income separately.

programmes.source_snippet: The Public Prescription Drug Insurance Plan covers persons who do not have access to a private plan; the amount of the annual premium varies according to net family income.

programmes.name_local: Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH)
programmes.name_en: Alberta Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH)
programmes.amount_note: Maximum living allowance $1,901/month (2024, indexed annually) for Albertans with a permanent medical condition severely limiting ability to work, plus health benefits (drugs, dental, optical) for the household. Alberta is transitioning new applicants toward the Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP).

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or with the paper AISH application
Have your physician complete the medical report
Financial eligibility (income/assets) is assessed after medical approval

documents_required.doc: Medical report completed by a physician

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested (assets up to $100,000 exempt)

programmes.source_snippet: AISH provides a maximum monthly living allowance of $1,901 to eligible Albertans with a severe and permanent disability, plus health benefits and personal benefits.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly financial assistance for food, clothing and shelter for Albertans who do not have the resources to meet basic needs; amount varies by household size, employability and situation, with employment services attached.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via your Alberta.ca account or at an Alberta Supports office
Provide income, asset and household information; meet with a caseworker

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: Income Support can help you and your family with basic needs like food, clothing and shelter if you do not have enough money.

programmes.funder: Government of Alberta (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: Quarterly benefit for lower- and middle-income families with children under 18: a base component and a working component, with amounts per child (higher for the first child) phased out by family net income; combined federal-provincial payment schedule.

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return and be registered for the CCB
Payments are calculated and issued automatically each quarter

eligibility.income_note: Income-tested on adjusted family net income; working component requires family working income

programmes.source_snippet: The ACFB is a tax-free amount paid to families that have children under 18 years of age; it is made up of a base component and a working component.

programmes.amount_note: Up to $3,792/year (2024-25, indexed) for low-income seniors 65+ (single), or up to $5,688 for couples, based on OAS/GIS receipt and accommodation type; paid monthly or quarterly.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or by mail after starting OAS (and ideally GIS)

eligibility.income_note: Alberta publishes, for the 1 July 2026 - 30 June 2027 benefit year, income guidelines of $32,690 or less for a single senior and $53,800 or less combined for a senior couple. Alberta notes these are guidelines only for seniors receiving the full OAS pension; actual entitlement varies with accommodation type, marital status and allowable deductions.

programmes.source_snippet: The Alberta Seniors Benefit provides a monthly benefit to eligible seniors with low-income to assist with living expenses.

programmes.name_en: City of Calgary Fair Entry (low-income programs access)
programmes.amount_note: Single application giving low-income Calgarians access to multiple subsidized City programs: Calgary Transit low-income transit pass (sliding scale by income), recreation fee assistance, property tax assistance, seniors services home maintenance and more.
programmes.deadline_note: Approval is valid for a set period; reapply when notified.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online, in person or by mail with income documents
Once approved, activate the specific subsidies (e.g., low-income transit pass) you need

eligibility.income_note: The City of Calgary publishes a Fair Entry eligibility table based on the Statistics Canada Low Income Cut-Off; the maximum total household income for a 1-person household is $31,906, rising with household size.

programmes.source_snippet: Fair Entry is an application process that helps Calgarians access City of Calgary subsidized programs and services, using one application for multiple programs.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly basic needs and shelter assistance for Manitobans with no or low income, including a stream for persons with disabilities; amounts vary by household size and category, with health benefits (dental, optical, prescriptions) included.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your local EIA office or online pre-application
Attend an intake interview and provide financial documentation

documents_required.doc: Income, asset and shelter cost information

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: The Employment and Income Assistance Program (EIA) provides financial help to Manitobans who have no other way to support themselves or their families.

programmes.amount_note: Monthly shelter benefit for low-income Manitobans renting in the private market (including EIA recipients and working households); based on income, rent paid and household size, paid automatically to eligible EIA households and on application to others.

procedure_steps.detail: EIA recipients: Rent Assist is assessed automatically
Non-EIA renters: apply with the Rent Assist application form and provide rent and income proof

eligibility.income_note: For Manitobans not receiving EIA, Manitoba requires a net annual income of less than $29,120 for a single person, or $33,920 for a single person 55 years of age or older, or a person who qualifies for the Disability Tax Credit or receives CPP Disability benefits. Limits are higher for larger households.

programmes.source_snippet: Rent Assist is a monthly shelter-related financial benefit to help low-income Manitobans who pay rent in the private market.

programmes.name_en: Manitoba 55 PLUS (income supplement for low-income Manitobans 55+)
programmes.amount_note: Quarterly income supplement for low-income Manitobans aged 55 and over who are not receiving EIA; single component for singles not yet on OAS/GIS and a senior component topping up low OAS incomes.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply with the 55 PLUS application form (online or paper)

documents_required.doc: Proof of age and Manitoba residence

eligibility.income_note: Manitoba 55 PLUS Junior component: annual income up to $9,746.40 for a single person and $16,255.20 for a couple. The Senior component instead tests family composition, net family income and the level of federal Old Age Security benefits received, and publishes no single maximum.

programmes.source_snippet: The 55 PLUS Program provides quarterly income supplements to low-income Manitobans who are 55 years of age and over.

programmes.funder: Government of Saskatchewan (Ministry of Social Services)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly income assistance with basic benefit, shelter benefit (actual rent up to caps by community) and utility benefits for low-income Saskatchewan residents; higher rates in northern communities.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or call the Client Service Centre
Provide income, asset, shelter and utility cost information

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling published. Saskatchewan states applicants must have no income or low income and have explored every other reasonable way to support themselves, using a whole-income approach in benefit calculation, but gives no dollar figure.

programmes.source_snippet: The Saskatchewan Income Support (SIS) program helps people meet their basic needs while they become more self-sufficient and independent to the best of their abilities.

programmes.funder: Government of Saskatchewan (Ministry of Social Services)
programmes.amount_note: Income support for people with significant and enduring disabilities: living income benefit, disability impact benefit, shelter benefit (actual costs up to caps) and northern supplement; designed to be more generous than SIS.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through the Ministry of Social Services
Provide medical documentation of a significant and enduring disability

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested; higher exemptions than SIS

programmes.source_snippet: The Saskatchewan Assured Income for Disability (SAID) program provides income support to people with significant and enduring disabilities.

programmes.funder: Government of Nova Scotia (Department of Opportunities and Social Development)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly basic needs (standard household rate) plus shelter allowance for Nova Scotians in financial need; higher rates for persons with disabilities; employment support services attached.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply by phone or in person at your local office
Complete the intake interview and provide financial documents

documents_required.doc: Income, asset and shelter cost information

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: Income Assistance provides financial support to Nova Scotians who cannot meet their basic needs.

programmes.funder: Government of Nova Scotia (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: Tax-free monthly payment of $127.08/month per child (2025-26, about $1,525/year) for low- and modest-income families with children under 18; paid with the federal CCB.

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return and be registered for the CCB
The NSCB is paid automatically with the CCB

eligibility.income_note: Full amount at AFNI under $26,000; partial between $26,000 and $34,000

programmes.source_snippet: The Nova Scotia Child Benefit is a non-taxable amount paid monthly to help low- and modest-income families with the cost of raising children under 18.

programmes.name_local: Nova Scotia Affordable Living Tax Credit (NSALTC)
programmes.name_en: Nova Scotia Affordable Living Tax Credit
programmes.funder: Government of Nova Scotia (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: Tax-free quarterly payment of $255/year per adult and $60 per child for low- and modest-income Nova Scotians, paid with the GST/HST credit.

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return
Payment is issued automatically with the GST/HST credit

eligibility.income_note: Reduced when adjusted family net income exceeds $30,000; eliminated at higher incomes

programmes.source_snippet: The Nova Scotia affordable living tax credit is a tax-free amount paid to make life more affordable for low and modest incomes; $255 for individuals and couples plus $60 for each child.

programmes.funder: Government of New Brunswick (Department of Social Development)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly assistance (transitional, interim and extended benefits streams) for basic needs of low-income New Brunswickers; single employable rate historically around $600/month, higher for persons with disabilities.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your regional Social Development office or by phone
Complete the eligibility interview and provide financial documents

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: The Social Assistance Program helps eligible individuals and families meet their basic needs when they are unable to do so themselves.

programmes.funder: Government of New Brunswick (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: Non-taxable payment of $250/year per child for low-income families, plus a working income supplement (up to $250) and school supply supplement for children born 2004+; paid with the CCB.

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return and be registered for the CCB
Payment is issued automatically with the CCB

eligibility.income_note: Full benefit at family net income up to $20,000; reduced above

programmes.source_snippet: The New Brunswick child tax benefit is a non-taxable amount paid monthly to qualifying families with children under 18 years of age; $250 annually for each child.

programmes.funder: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador (Department of Children, Seniors and Social Development)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly assistance for basic needs, shelter and utilities for residents with no or insufficient income; includes a disability stream and support for seniors and families in need.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through your local Income Support office
Provide identification and financial documentation

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: Income Support provides financial benefits and other services to eligible low-income people to assist in meeting daily living expenses.

programmes.funder: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador (administered by the CRA)
programmes.amount_note: Non-taxable monthly amount paid with the CCB to low- and modest-income families with children under 18; per-child amounts vary by birth order and are phased out by family net income (mother's nutrition supplement also included).

procedure_steps.detail: File your income tax return and be registered for the CCB
Payment is issued automatically with the CCB

eligibility.income_note: CRA publishes only the phase-out start, not a hard ceiling: for July 2026 - June 2027 the maximum is $157.33/month for the first child, and above an adjusted family net income of $20,397 you may get part of the benefit. The zero point depends on the number of children and is not published.

programmes.source_snippet: The Newfoundland and Labrador child benefit is a non-taxable amount paid monthly to help low-income families with the cost of raising children under 18 years of age.

programmes.name_en: Prince Edward Island Social Assistance Program
programmes.funder: Government of Prince Edward Island (Department of Social Development and Seniors)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly assistance for food, shelter and basic needs for Islanders unable to meet them through other means; rates set by household size and include disability supports.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through a Social Assistance office
Provide identification, income and asset documentation

eligibility.income_note: Income and asset tested

programmes.source_snippet: Social Assistance helps Prince Edward Island residents meet their basic needs when they are unable to provide for themselves.

programmes.name_en: City of Vancouver Leisure Access Program
programmes.amount_note: Free or 50%-reduced admission to Park Board pools, rinks and fitness centres plus discounts on registered programs for low-income Vancouver residents; card valid one year.
programmes.deadline_note: Card valid for one year; reapply annually.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at a community centre with proof of income/residency
Use the Leisure Access card at Park Board facilities

documents_required.doc: Proof of low income (NOA or assistance documentation)

eligibility.income_note: Vancouver publishes Leisure Access Program net-family-income tables: the general low-income table is $43,028 for a 1-person household, and $53,166 for households where someone receives the Disability Tax Credit or Child Disability Benefit. Thresholds rise with family size.

programmes.source_snippet: The Leisure Access Program helps low-income residents access Park Board programs and services at reduced cost.

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt canadien pour la formation
programmes.amount_note: Refundable tax credit covering 50% of eligible tuition/fees, up to a $250 annual accumulation ($5,000 lifetime) for workers aged 26-65 with income in the eligible range (roughly $10,000 to the top of the second bracket).
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on the annual tax return against training taken in the year.

procedure_steps.detail: Accumulate training credit limit (shown on your Notice of Assessment)
Claim the credit on your tax return for eligible course fees

documents_required.doc: Tuition receipts (T2202) from an eligible educational institution

eligibility.income_note: Working income of at least ~$10,000 and net income below the top of the second federal bracket

programmes.source_snippet: The Canada Training Credit is a refundable tax credit to help Canadians with the cost of eligible training fees; you accumulate $250 each year you are eligible, up to a lifetime limit of $5,000.

programmes.amount_note: Non-refundable credit of 15% on up to $20,000 of eligible renovation expenses (max $3,000) to make a home safer/more accessible for a senior (65+) or a person eligible for the Disability Tax Credit.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on line 31285 of the annual tax return.

procedure_steps.detail: Complete qualifying renovations to an eligible dwelling
Keep receipts and claim up to $20,000 on line 31285 of your return

documents_required.doc: DTC approval or proof of age 65+

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested

programmes.source_snippet: The home accessibility tax credit is a non-refundable tax credit for qualifying expenses incurred for work performed or goods acquired in respect of a qualifying renovation of an eligible dwelling.

programmes.name_local: Crédit d'impôt pour la rénovation d'habitations multigénérationnelles
programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit of 15% on up to $50,000 of renovation costs (max $7,500) to create a self-contained secondary unit for a senior or a DTC-eligible adult relative to live with family.
programmes.deadline_note: One qualifying renovation per eligible person; claimed in the year the renovation is completed.

procedure_steps.detail: Build a self-contained secondary unit for the qualifying relative
Claim up to $50,000 of expenses on line 45355 of your return

documents_required.doc: Proof of relationship and the relative's age or DTC status

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested

programmes.source_snippet: The MHRTC is a refundable tax credit that can be claimed for eligible renovation expenses to create a self-contained secondary unit for a qualifying relation to live with a qualifying individual.

programmes.name_local: Déduction pour frais de garde d'enfants
programmes.amount_note: Deduct eligible child care costs from income: up to $8,000 per child under 7, $5,000 per child 7-16, and $11,000 per child eligible for the Disability Tax Credit; generally claimed by the lower-income spouse.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed on form T778 with the annual tax return.

procedure_steps.detail: Keep receipts from your child care provider (daycare, camps, sitters)
Complete form T778 and claim the deduction on your return

documents_required.doc: Child care receipts with the provider's SIN/business number

eligibility.income_note: Deduction capped at 2/3 of earned income for most claimants

programmes.source_snippet: Child care expenses are amounts you paid to have someone look after an eligible child so that you could earn income, go to school, or conduct research.

programmes.name_local: Remboursement de la TPS/TVH pour habitations neuves
programmes.amount_note: Rebate of part of the GST (or federal part of HST) paid on a new or substantially renovated home bought from a builder, built by the owner, or purchased as a co-op share; provincial rebates (e.g., Ontario) can add up to $24,000.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply within 2 years of the purchase/closing.

procedure_steps.detail: Complete the applicable rebate form (GST190/GST191 or RC7000 for Ontario)
Submit with purchase documents to the CRA

documents_required.doc: Agreement of purchase and sale / statement of adjustments

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; purchase price caps apply to the federal portion ($450,000)

programmes.source_snippet: You may be eligible for a new housing rebate for some of the GST/HST paid if you purchased a new or substantially renovated house from a builder, built your own house, or substantially renovated your own house.

programmes.funder: Employment and Social Development Canada (Service Canada)
programmes.amount_note: Monthly pension for the surviving spouse/common-law partner of a deceased CPP contributor: max $904.59/month if 65+ (January 2026), $803.54 if under 65; children's benefit $307.81/month.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or with form ISP1300 after the contributor's death

documents_required.doc: Death certificate or proof of death
Social Insurance Numbers of both spouses

eligibility.income_note: Contributory benefit; combined-benefit rules cap total CPP amounts

programmes.source_snippet: Survivor's pension - 65 and older: maximum $904.59 per month; younger than 65: $803.54 (January 2026).

programmes.name_en: Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) for First Nations and Inuit
programmes.amount_note: Covers eligible drugs, dental care, vision care, mental health counselling, medical transportation and medical supplies/equipment for registered First Nations and recognized Inuit not otherwise covered.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm eligibility (status card or Inuit recognition) and register with NIHB
Use enrolled providers who bill NIHB directly

documents_required.doc: Certificate of Indian Status or Inuit enrolment proof

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; based on First Nations status or Inuit recognition

programmes.source_snippet: The Non-Insured Health Benefits program provides eligible First Nations and Inuit clients with coverage for a range of health benefits that are not covered through other programs.

programmes.amount_note: Temporary health coverage (basic, supplemental and prescription drug benefits) for refugee claimants, resettled refugees and certain protected persons until they qualify for provincial health insurance.
programmes.deadline_note: Coverage is temporary; ends when provincial coverage or status resolution takes effect.

procedure_steps.detail: IFHP coverage is issued with your refugee claim or resettlement documents
Use IFHP-registered providers (search via Medavie Blue Cross)

documents_required.doc: Refugee Protection Claimant Document or IRCC-issued eligibility document

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested

programmes.source_snippet: The Interim Federal Health Program provides limited, temporary coverage of health-care benefits to people in Canada who are not yet eligible for provincial or territorial health insurance.

programmes.amount_note: Ensures First Nations children can access the health, social and educational products, services and supports they need, when they need them; funding approved case-by-case at no cost to the family.

procedure_steps.detail: Call the Jordan's Principle call centre (1-855-JP-CHILD) or contact a regional focal point
Submit the request with supporting documents (professional recommendation)

documents_required.doc: Professional recommendation for the needed service/support
Proof of First Nations child eligibility

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; for First Nations children on or off reserve

programmes.source_snippet: Jordan's Principle makes sure all First Nations children living in Canada can access the products, services and supports they need, when they need them.

programmes.name_local: Allocation pour études et formation des vétérans
programmes.amount_note: Up to ~$86,720 for veterans with 12+ years of service (or ~$43,360 with 6+ years) toward tuition and costs of college, university or technical education after release from the Canadian Armed Forces.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply within 10 years of release.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via My VAC Account
Enrol in an eligible program; funds are paid in annual installments

documents_required.doc: Proof of CAF service and release date
Proof of enrolment in an eligible program

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested; based on years of CAF service

programmes.source_snippet: The Education and Training Benefit is a taxable benefit that provides funding to Veterans to achieve their education and career goals after release.
